page: Amazon Web Services x1e.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hardware includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 122.0 GB of total RAM, which equals 30.5 GB per vCPU. Accelerators are omitted, with zero GPUs present. Storage is provisioned via a bundled 120 GB local solid-state drive, accompanied by a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute and transfer constraints typical of this hardware generation. In stress-ng testing, the platform records 735.49 in single-core and 2070.55 in multi-core metrics, falling into lower performance percentiles. Geekbench testing mirrors this, scoring 833.0 in single-core and 1767.0 in multi-core execution. Memory throughput measurements yield 19.06 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 13.67 GB/sec for uncached writes, contrasting with 156.24 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read operations. Application metrics include 2.37 million Redis SET operations per second, 2.7 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 52.5 tokens per second for small-model 135M text generation.

From a resource allocation standpoint, the system trades raw processing speed and modern instruction extensions for high memory density per core, lacking AVX-512 support. The substantial memory footprint caters to applications whose active data sets exceed typical memory boundaries, making CPU performance a secondary priority. Consequently, the instance is engineered primarily for in-memory database deployments, enterprise caching systems, and ETL pipelines that require large working sets in RAM without requiring modern parallel compute throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services x1e.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor, engineered for workloads requiring high memory capacity relative to compute resources. The system is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, supported by 45 MB of L3 cache. It features 122.0 GB of system memory, delivering 30.5 GB per vCPU, along with a 120 GB local SSD and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. It contains no GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate modest processing throughput, with Geekbench scores of 833.0 single-core and 1767.0 multi-core, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 19.06 GB/sec. Given its disproportionate memory ratio and legacy architecture, this instance is suited for memory-bound applications, including in-memory databases, large caching layers, and analytical workloads where RAM capacity outweighs execution speed.
